extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, third-party protestors, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for preparing, filing, and handling protests submitted to the USPTO under 37 CFR 1.291, including eligibility, timing, required contents, service, examiner treatment, and limits on protestor participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Can Protest / Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the public, including private persons, corporate entities, and government agencies, may file a protest under 37 CFR 1.291. A protest may be filed by an attorney or other representative on behalf of an unnamed real party in interest; 37 CFR 1.291 does not require identification of the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement must accompany the protest that it is the first protest submitted in the application by the real party in interest who is submitting the protest, unless the protest complies with 37 CFR 1.291(c)(5). The requirements of 1.291(c)(5) cannot be avoided by multiple protests submitted by different people representing the same real party in interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of Protest
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest must be filed prior to the date the application is published under 37 CFR 1.211 or the date a notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.311 is given or mailed, whichever occurs first, except that a protest accompanied by the written consent of the applicant may be considered if filed prior to the date a notice of allowance is given or mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests filed on or after publication (without applicant consent) will not be entered. Publication under PCT or certain international registrations does not trigger the end of the 1.291(b) period for national stage applications. Protests may not be filed in provisional applications. For reissue applications, protests may be filed throughout pendency prior to allowance but are ideally filed within the 2-month period after announcement in the Official Gazette; petitions under 37 CFR 1.182 and fees may be needed in special circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information List — required identification of submitted items (37 CFR 1.291(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Protest must include an information list of the documents, portions of documents, or other information being submitted where each item is identified in a specific manner: (i) U.S. patents by patent number, first named inventor, and issue date; (ii) U.S. patent application publications by publication number, first named inventor, and publication date; (iii) foreign patents/published foreign applications by country/office, appropriate document number, applicant/patentee/first named inventor, and publication date; (iv) non-patent publications by author (if any), title, pages submitted, publication date, and where available publisher/place; (v) other items identified by date, if known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.291(c)(1)(iv) does not preclude providing additional identifying information (e.g., journal title and volume). Flexibility is permitted for foreign documents and non-patent literature when some information is unavailable. If a document portion is listed, submit that portion plus pages providing identifying information (cover, title page, copyright).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise Explanation of Relevance (37 CFR 1.291(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the relevance of each item identified in the information list must accompany the protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations should tie each cited item to why the item would make grant of a patent improper (e.g., anticipatory prior art, obviousness, public use/sale, inventorship, 35 U.S.C. 112 issues). Major arguments should be clear so the examiner can consider and respond to the main points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of Submitted Items (37 CFR 1.291(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A legible copy of each item identified in the information list must be provided, other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only a portion of a document is listed, submit only that portion plus any pages that provide identifying information (e.g., cover, title page, copyright). A protest not accompanied by copies of each relied-on document (except as exempted) will not be entered; protestor will not be given an opportunity to supplement incomplete protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: English Translation Requirement (37 CFR 1.291(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: An English language translation of any non-English language item identified in the information list must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required translation may be a reliable machine translation and need not be certified. If only a portion of a non-English document is submitted, only translate that portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second or Subsequent Protest Requirements (37 CFR 1.291(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the protest is a second or subsequent protest by the same real party in interest, it must include: (1) an explanation why the issue(s) raised are significantly different than those raised earlier; (2) an explanation why the significantly different issue(s) were not presented earlier; and (3) the processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significantly different issues are typically new, non-cumulative prior art or information not previously made of record. Additional comments or further data on previously raised issues do not qualify. Multiple protests filed by different people representing the same real party cannot circumvent these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service / Filing Requirements (37 CFR 1.291(b) and 1.248)
rubrics_metrics.description: The protest must be served upon the applicant in accordance with 37 CFR 1.248, or filed with the Office in duplicate if service is not possible. The protest filed with the Office must reflect that a copy has been served or be filed in duplicate for forwarding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service methods under 1.248 include personal delivery, leaving at business with an employee, leaving at residence with a suitable person, first-class mail (date of mailing = date of service), or published notice if other modes impracticable. Proof of service must include date and manner; personal service must include name of person served certified by server. If filing duplicate because service is impossible, include an explanation why service could not be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest must specifically identify the application to which it is directed by application number or serial number and filing date, and be as complete as possible in identifying the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, include on the first page: name of inventor(s); name of applicant(s); application number; filing date; title of invention; art unit number (if known); name of examiner (if known). Insufficient identification can lead to the protest not being matched or being returned/discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Format and Where to File
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest must be submitted in writing and must NOT be submitted electronically via EFS-Web. Protests can be mailed to Mail Stop Petition, Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each protest should be clearly identified as a 'PROTEST UNDER 37 CFR 1.291.' If the protestor cannot identify the specific application by number, the protest should be directed to the Office of Petitions with as much identifying data as possible. Reissue litigation protests should be conspicuously marked 'REISSUE LITIGATION' on the envelope and top right-hand corner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of Protest
rubrics_metrics.description: A member of the public filing a protest will not receive communications from the Office relating to the protest other than the return of a self-addressed postcard if included with the protest in order to receive an acknowledgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt of the self-addressed postcard does not indicate that the protest complies with 37 CFR 1.291. The postcard for an original or reissue application will not indicate whether the application exists or its status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest submission must be complete and contain a copy of every document relied on by the protestor (except U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete protests will not be entered and the protestor will not be given an opportunity to supplement or complete them. Active participation by protestor ends with the filing; further submissions will not be considered unless under 37 CFR 1.291(c)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Evidence That May Be Relied On
rubrics_metrics.description: Any information which, in the protestor’s opinion, would make the grant of a patent improper can be relied on. Examples include prior art documents, information demonstrating public knowledge or use, public use or sale, abandonment of invention, inventorship issues, compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112, fraud or violation of duty of disclosure, and other facts adverse to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence may include court litigation materials (complaints, answers, depositions, exhibits, transcripts, court orders), affidavits or declarations for public use/sale evidence (orders, invoices, delivery schedules), and trade secret information (submitted per MPEP §724). Protestors must recognize potential problems of authentication and probative value; Office will evaluate each item and assign weight accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade Secret / Protected Material Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Information subject to a court-imposed protective or secrecy order, or trade secret information obtained via agreements, may be submitted with or as part of a protest but must be submitted in accordance with MPEP §724.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protected/secret material submitted per MPEP §724 will be treated as set forth therein and will be made public if a reasonable examiner would consider the information important in deciding whether to allow the application. Follow MPEP §724 procedures to ensure the Office recognizes the protection claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Office Review and Entry Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests will be reviewed by designated points of contact and procedures to determine compliance with 37 CFR 1.291 before being made of record. A protest that fails to comply with 1.291(b) or (c) may not be entered; however, minor errors that do not raise ambiguity may be overlooked at the Office's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an error is minor but content is ascertainable (e.g., misspelled inventor name but correct patent number and issue date), the Office may enter the protest. The Office will either enter or not enter the entire protest and will not generally attempt to enter portions of partially compliant protests. If an examiner believes a protest is non-compliant, the examiner should consult the reviewer; documents deemed not to be considered may be stricken with notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Treatment — Consideration of Submitted Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If entered in time to permit consideration, the examiner must consider each of the prior art or other documents submitted in conformance with 37 CFR 1.291(c) and any discussion of such documents in the protest, and any non-prior art issues appropriate for primary examiner consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must conduct a normal examination and required search. Prior art relied on in rejecting claims will be made of record by PTO-892 or by initialing the PTO/SB/08A/08B form; otherwise the examiner will annotate the protest paper as 'checked' with initials. The next Office action should indicate that all documents submitted have been considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Response to Protestor's Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Office action by the examiner treating the merits of a timely submitted protest complying with 37 CFR 1.291(c) must specifically consider and make evident by detailed reasoning the examiner's position as to the major arguments and points raised by the protestor, except for issues related to inequitable conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary to respond to every minute argument, but major arguments (other than fraud/inequitable conduct) must be specifically covered. Arguments concerning 'fraud' or 'duty of disclosure' are generally not discussed by the Office, though such protests will be entered in the file generally without comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Comment Period and Required Replies (37 CFR 1.291(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office's initial review shows a protest is ready for consideration, the examiner may offer the applicant an opportunity to file comments (usually 1 month) and may require the applicant to reply to the protest and answer specific questions under 37 CFR 1.291(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs (e.g., 19.01 and 19.02) may be used to offer a comment period and to require information. The primary examiner cannot require a reply to questions relating to fraud, inequitable conduct, or duty of disclosure. Failure by applicant to reply to a required information request may result in abandonment under standard statutory periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protestor Participation Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The protestor's participation ends with the filing of the protest; protestors will not be allowed to communicate with or receive information from the Office regarding disposition or status of the protest or application, will not be served Office actions, and cannot participate in interviews or appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protestor cannot appeal an examiner decision adverse to the protestor to the PTAB or otherwise participate in applicant's appeals. If protestor has access to an application (e.g., certain reissue applications open to public), the protestor may monitor proceedings to the extent permitted by access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple / Piecemeal Protests Prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.291(c) does not permit submission of additional protests in the same application by the same real party in interest except pursuant to 37 CFR 1.291(c)(5). Multiple piecemeal protests raising slightly different issues in each submission by the same real party in interest are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second or subsequent protests that do not comply with c(5) will not be entered and may be returned or discarded. Compliant second/subsequent protests must be timely, significantly different (non-cumulative) and include required explanations and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Non-Compliant or Improper Protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests that fail to comply with 37 CFR 1.291(b) or (c) may not be entered; if not entered they will be returned to the protestor or discarded at the Office's option. Improper protests will be returned or discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where errors are minor and content ascertainable, the Office may nevertheless enter the protest. If a protest cannot be adequately matched to an application in time for examiner review due to inadequate identification, it may not be entered and may be returned or discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Rules for Reissue Application Protests
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest filed in a reissue application is not a 'form of preissuance opposition' and may be filed in the reissue application throughout its pendency prior to notice of allowance, subject to examination timing. A protest with regard to a reissue application should be filed within the 2-month period following announcement of the filing of the reissue application in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a protest cannot be filed within the 2-month period, it can be submitted later, but may be received after action by the examiner; petitions under 37 CFR 1.182 with fee under 1.17(f) may be required to extend or to have the protest considered where prosecution on the merits has been closed or final rejection issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portions of Documents and Identifying Pages
rubrics_metrics.description: When only a portion of a document is listed as an item in the information list, only a copy of that portion must be submitted along with copies of pages of the document that provide identifying information (e.g., cover, title page, copyright information page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces submission burden but ensures the Office can identify the source. Similar rule applies to non-English documents—the portion and its translation suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine Translations Allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: The required English language translation of any non-English item of information may be a reliable machine translation and need not be certified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliability of machine translation is acceptable; no certification or notarization required. Translate only submitted portions if partial submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Prior Art Under 37 CFR 1.501(a) (note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separately, 37 CFR 1.501(a) permits any person at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent to file written submissions of prior art (patents and printed publications) pertinent to a patent; see MPEP §2202–§2208.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a different mechanism from pre-issuance protests (37 CFR 1.291) and may be appropriate for post-issue prior art submissions.
